content.text: Japanese Mahjong, or Riichi Mahjong, is the most competitively evolved form of the Chinese classic. It is characterized by the 'Riichi' mechanicâ€”a declaration of being one card away from winningâ€”and the 'Dora' system of bonus point cards. It is a highly defensive and strategic game where 'not losing' (avoiding dealing into an opponent's hand) is as important as winning.
Mahjong was introduced to Japan in the early 1900s. After WWII, the rules were standardized into the 'Riichi' style to facilitate national tournaments.
136 tiles: 3 suits (1-9), Winds, Dragons. One 'Dora' indicator is turned over in the dead wall.

Each player starts with 13 tiles; dealer with 14.

items.text: Hanchan (Half game): Standard format: East and South rounds; game ends after South round. Used in most tournaments and online play.
Tonpuusen (East-only): Only East round is played; faster format used in some casual and league settings.
Aka Dora (Red fives): One or more red 5 tiles per suit count as Dora and add bonus value when in hand or as Dora indicator.
